candidates.name: inn-hotels-booking-cancellation-prediction
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSV Data/INNHotelsGroup.csv from the 'INN Hotels Group' academic dataset (India-based hotel chain, coursework-sourced, commonly cited as ~36,275 bookings). Fields include lead_time (days between booking and arrival), arrival date parts, market_segment_type, room_type_reserved, avg_price_per_room, no_of_special_requests, repeated_guest, deposit_type, and booking_status (Canceled/Not_Canceled).
candidates.why_useful: A second, independently-sourced hotel booking-lead-time + cancellation-outcome dataset (different market/vendor than the Portugal H1/H2 Antonio dataset already held) — useful for cross-checking lead-time distributions and cancellation-rate base rates against a different hotel chain/geography (targets gap #3, RNPL/cancellation thesis, as a comparator, not a duplicate of the Portugal file).
candidates.license: unclear (repo states dataset rights remain with original academic provider; code appears MIT/unspecified)
candidates.time_coverage: unspecified (coursework dataset, no explicit date range surfaced)
candidates.size_hint: ~36k rows (per widely-cited version of this dataset; not independently row-counted in this pass)

candidates.name: airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Tom Slee's pre-Inside-Airbnb scraper/database schema for surveying Airbnb search-page listings city by city into a PostgreSQL 'room' table (bounding-box searches, room ids, availability, price flags). README (fetched) does not itself surface where historic collected-data dumps are hosted; maintainer states in 2019 they stopped maintaining it. No cancellation-policy field confirmed in the excerpt fetched.
candidates.why_useful: If Tom Slee's own historic data dumps (2015-2017, many world cities) survive anywhere (his old site or a mirror), they would be an independent pre-2023 Airbnb listings source, addressing gap #1 (historical Inside-Airbnb-era coverage) — but this GitHub repo itself is only the scraper method, is unmaintained since 2019, and running it against airbnb.com is out of policy for us per repo rules (non-sanctioned scrape target).
candidates.time_coverage: ~2015-2017 surveys (per public knowledge of the project; not independently confirmed in this pass)
candidates.size_hint: unknown; scraper code only in this repo, no committed CSVs seen
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: adjacent to Inside Airbnb historical gap, not a duplicate of anything currently held

candidates.name: vrbo-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed scraper (2 commits) targeting Vrbo.com, configured per-city via cities.vrbo.json; extracts 30+ fields per property including price, room configuration, amenities, host info, and cancellation policy, plus up to 12 images. No sample data confirmed committed to the repo itself.
candidates.why_useful: A working method to pull Vrbo cancellation-policy and pricing fields at the listing level would speak to gap #9 (competitor/adjacent supply) and give a comparator for cancellation-policy mix outside Airbnb, but this repo is minimal (2 commits), unverified at scale, and scraping Vrbo directly is a method only — not run in this pass.
candidates.geography: configurable, example shown for Bogota, Colombia
candidates.time_coverage: n/a (live scrape method, not a stored dataset)

candidates.name: Hotel-Cancellation-Minimization-Booking-Behavior-Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Re-analysis (Power BI .pbix + notes) of the same well-known Kaggle 'hotel_booking_demand' dataset (Antonio/Almeida/Nunes, ~100k+ records, Jul 2015-Oct 2017) already held, with a window_booking (lead time) and booking_status field surfaced explicitly in the writeup.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the Portugal H1/H2 dataset is the dominant public hotel-cancellation source on GitHub and that its lead-time field is literally named 'window_booking' in some derivative repos — useful only as a pointer to the same data we already hold, not new.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Portugal hotel-booking demand dataset (Antonio/Almeida/Nunes) already in our holdings

notes: This modality was largely non-functional for this run: WebSearch reported its session-wide quota (200/200) already exhausted before any of my calls executed (likely consumed by other parallel scout agents sharing the same session budget) so zero WebSearch queries actually ran; github.com/search (the web UI) returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, consistent with the instruction that gh/GitHub search is being hammered by other agents in this sweep; Bing via WebFetch returned generic, query-ignoring results (its site: operator and multi-term queries were not honored by whatever renders the page for WebFetch); DuckDuckGo HTML search served a CAPTCHA both times; Hugging Face's dataset search page and Zenodo's web search page are JS-rendered and returned no results via WebFetch (Zenodo's REST API at /api/records did work and was used instead). Given all of that, I fell back to GitHub's static /topics/<tag> pages (which did render) and to direct repo/README fetches for names recalled from training knowledge. Bottom line on substance: the cancellation/lead-time/RNPL theme is thin on GitHub specifically — almost everything indexed under hotel-cancellation, booking-cancellation, and hotel-booking-demand topics is yet another ML-tutorial re-analysis of the same two academic datasets (the Portugal H1/H2 set we already hold, and to a lesser extent the India 'INN Hotels' set, which is new to us and worth a line). No RNPL-specific dataset, no STR PMS (AirDNA/Key Data/Guesty/Hospitable) open cancellation data, and no Airbnb-specific cancellation-rate dataset surfaced anywhere in this pass; 'airdna' and 'expedia-hotel-recommendations' GitHub topics are literally empty. Suggest a re-run of this theme once GitHub web search rate-limiting clears, and/or a gh-CLI pass (not available to this modality) which would likely surface more than topic pages did. Also worth a follow-up scout specifically on PMS vendor developer docs (Guesty, Hospitable, Hostaway, Cloudbeds) for any public sample/sandbox cancellation data, and on airline/cruise 'book-ahead' lead-time datasets (gap #18) which I did not get to due to tool failures eating most of the budget.
